subject: Priority: NovaRetail capacity hit — throughput shortfall causing latency & errors
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novaretail.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Rivera <monica.rivera@novaretail.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production impact — sudden throughput shortfall and spikes in latency/errors

Hey Aditya,

We started seeing significant 95p+ latency spikes and an uptick in 500/503 errors on our inference route (model: rwd-large-v1, pinned) starting ~08:45 PDT. Traffic volume hasn't changed on our end — same QPS — but end-to-end latencies jumped from ~120ms to >1.2s and error rate climbed to ~3.8%. This is affecting checkout personalization during our morning traffic window.

Attached is a small bundle with request/response traces and stack samples (novaretail-error-log-20260929.zip). Please escalate — our SRE is standing by and this is visible to our product/ops leadership.

Key ask: immediate triage and temporary capacity relief. We need an ETA for mitigation and a timeline for preventing recurrence.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Engineering, NovaRetail
liam.oconnor@novaretail.com
+1 415-555-0198

I'll stay on this until it's resolved.

On Tue, Sep 29, 2026 at 09:25 AM Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Initial plan (short): Naomi to give a telemetry read...

Hi all — I pulled live telemetry and a few quick observations:

1) Dedicated pool utilization: GPU occupancy across the pool for NovaRetail's reservation is at 98% aggregate; NVLink memory pressure and long KV-cache lifetimes on some long-context requests have increased token compute time per request.
2) No aggressive traffic spike on your QPS; the increase appears to be due to a small set (~4) of high-encoder-length batched jobs from an internal data pipeline that started at 08:30 PDT and is co-located on the same reserved nodes. These jobs are generating large decode windows and persistently keeping KV caches hot, preventing efficient batching for short requests.
3) Error correlation: most 500/503s map to queue timeouts when the pool runs out of free slots and fallback paths are exhausted.

Immediate mitigations we can enact now (0—45 min):
- Apply an emergency isolation policy: migrate the noisy pipeline jobs off your reserved pool to best-effort (will take ~7–12min).
- Expand reserved allocation by adding 2x burst instances (if we get approval from capacity control) — gives immediate headroom for ~20–30 minutes.
- Shorten KV cache TTL for your reservation (risk: slight perf regression for some large-context flows) — quick toggle (~3 min).
- Temporarily enable per-route short-circuit: send very long-encoder requests to a fallback model variant to avoid holding GPUs.

Next steps I'm executing now:
- Opening a capacity control request for a 2x burst and tagging it high priority.
- Starting migration of the identified pipeline jobs to best-effort — expecting migration completion in ~10 minutes.
- Pushing reduced KV TTL to 30s for your reservation as a short-term step.

I'll post another update in 15 minutes with concrete numbers and whether the 2x burst is approved. If burst is denied, we'll start a faster job-level throttling plan.

Naomi Feldman
Runtime Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

(Attachment: nr-telemetry-snapshot-09-29.json — 120 KB telemetry snapshot)

Thanks Naomi — and Aditya, please add me into the customer bridge.

Quick exec note: NovaRetail is a strategic mid-market account (annual committed reserved capacity). I want us to greenlight the burst if capacity control can honor it for the next 60 minutes and to prepare a small customer make-good.

Proposed customer facing response (sales-led):
- Immediate: authorize the 2x burst to stop the impact.
- Short term: waive one week of reserved fees for the impacted reservation as a goodwill credit.
- Long term: schedule a technical review with NovaRetail and offer a migration plan to isolate their heavy data-pipeline work or upgrade their reservation floor.

Vivek — can you OK the burst approval and sign the capacity request? If we need a formal SLA exception, I'll route it to Legal.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success & Sales Operations
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
